text:
mike: Quick spike proposal — instead of per-customer peering or per-tenant ENIs for Private control plane egress, what if we introduce a regional 'uplink consolidator' that aggregates outbound CP traffic and exposes a small number of stable egress IPs per region.
priya: curious — main win is fewer peering attachments?
mike: yep. fewer peering objects, much lower route churn, and easier NAT/inspection by customers. also reduces cross-account ENI quotas.
chen: tradeoff is that we'd centralize a critical path. single hop added and maybe higher blast radius. how do we keep latency and auth tight?
sam: we can keep mTLS all the way to the consolidator and use scoped tokens per customer. consolidator does auth & forwarding, not termination.
laura: what about cert rotation and audit logs? customers want proof their CP calls are isolated.
arjun: operator-side certificate per-customer, presented during the upstream TLS handshake. consolidator just proxies raw TLS when we want customer visibility. when we need app-level routing we terminate and re-establish inside a hardened cluster.
priya: so two modes: passthrough (preserve end-to-end mTLS) and terminate+reoriginate for policy/inspection. both supported by the consolidator.
mike: exactly. implement as: 
```
# rough config
region: us-west-2
mode: passthrough | terminate
egress_ips: [54.21.1.3, 54.21.1.4]
route_policy: customer -> consolidator -> controlplane
```
chen: ops questions: how do we handle IP preservation for customers who do source-IP map? consolidator will NAT; we can support NAT mapping table pinned per-customer but that gets stateful.
sam: we can offer sticky NAT for long-lived controlplane sessions and ephemeral NAT fallback for bursty ones. tie to session TTL and reconnect heuristics.
laura: rollout plan? start with low-risk customers in a single region, run consolidator behind existing peerings, and dual-write route tables for a canary.
arjun: also need a health and traffic shaping contract: max queueing delay, backpressure semantics, and fallback policy to direct peering if consolidator overloaded.
ops-bot: deploy-bot started: spike branch at https://git.redwood.internal/uplink-consolidator-spike, cluster smith/usc-aggregator created.
priya: nice. followups: (1) security review for terminate mode, (2) capacity model for NAT state, (3) migration playbook for per-customer peering -> consolidator.
mike: agreed. I'll draft an RFC with diagrams and the canary checklist. anyone want to own the security review?
laura: happy to. can take terminate-mode threat model and cert rotation notes.
chen: I'll do capacity calc and failure modes.
sam: I'll sketch fallback policies and metric set (p95 egress latency, nat table exhaustion, connection churn).
arjun: I'll draft the migration cutover playbook and runbook entries.
priya: sweet. keep the spike small and prefer passthrough first. :thumbsup:
